_meta.indication: VYEPTI is indicated for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study; patients randomized 1:1:1:1 to 30 mg, 100 mg, or 300 mg eptinezumab IV, or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18-75 years with at least a one-year history of migraine with or without aura, with 14 or fewer headache days per 28 days (at least 4 migraine days).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in the frequency of monthly migraine days over weeks 1-12.
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change from baseline in monthly migraine days: -4.29 (300 mg) and -3.88 (100 mg) vs -3.19 placebo; treatment effect -1.11 (p=0.0001) for 300 mg and -0.69 (p=0.0181) for 100 mg.

pivotal_trials.design: Identical in design to Study CLIN-006 except doses studied were 100 mg or 300 mg and the population was chronic migraine patients; double-blind placebo-controlled with primary endpoint at 12 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic migraine; 15 to 26 headache days a month, of which at least 8 were assessed as migraine days.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in monthly migraine days over weeks 1-12 (primary endpoint tested for the 300 mg dose).
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change from baseline in monthly migraine days: -8.2 (300 mg) and -7.7 (100 mg) vs -5.6 placebo; treatment effect -2.59 (p<0.0001) for 300 mg and -2.03 (p<0.0001) for 100 mg.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence at least 2% and at least 2% greater than placebo) were nasopharyngitis (100 mg 6%, 300 mg 8% vs placebo 6%) and hypersensitivity reactions (100 mg 1%, 300 mg 2% vs placebo 0%). In Studies 1 and 2, 1.9% of VYEPTI-treated patients discontinued because of adverse reactions.
target_moa: Eptinezumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds to the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) ligand and prevents CGRP binding to its receptor, blocking both alpha- and beta-CGRP isoforms.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the applicant had provided substantial evidence of effectiveness from two adequate and well-controlled studies and the safety profile was acceptable.

description.text: Added Clinical Studies data from Study 3 (NCT01719055) in adults candidates for preventive migraine treatment presenting with concurrent migraine on the day of infusion

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for inclusion of information in the Clinical Studies section of the Prescribing Information regarding Study 3 (NCT01719055), which enrolled adults who were candidates for preventive migraine treatment with VYEPTI and who presented with a concurrent migraine on the day of infusion.

summary.text: VYEPTI (eptinezumab-jjmr) was approved as a new biologics license application for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults, based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 studies (one in episodic and one in chronic migraine); the application was not referred to an advisory committee, and it was approved effective on the date of the approval letter with post-marketing requirements including pediatric and pregnancy outcome studies.

citations.quote: This review discusses the data presented by Lundbeck (the applicant) in support of a new biologics license application (BLA) for eptinezumab solution for intravenous (IV) injection, a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) inhibitor, proposed for the preventive treatment of migraine.

The efficacy of eptinezumab was demonstrated in two adequate and well-controlled studies, one study in patients with episodic migraine and one study in patients with chronic migraine. Both studies used a well-validated and clinically interpretable primary endpoint, the number of monthly migraine headache days. requirement.text: 3796-3: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, efficacy and safety study of eptinezumab in patients with episodic migraine age 6 through 17 years.

citations.quote: 3796-3 A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, efficacy and safety study of eptinezumab in patients with episodic migraine age 6 through 17 years. The study will include an initial double-blind treatment phase (minimum of 3 months) followed by an open-label extension phase for a minimum of 9 months duration. Of the total number of patients enrolled in this trial, a minimum of 25% of patients will be in the 6-11 year age group. There will be a similar number of patients in the 12-14 year old age range, and the 15-17 year old age range. This study is to be submitted as a Special Protocol Assessment (SPA).

requirement.text: 3796-5: Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with migraine exposed to Vyepti during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations.

citations.quote: 3796-5 Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with migraine exposed to Vypeti during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations: one consisting of women with migraine who have not been exposed to Vypeti before or during pregnancy, and the other consisting of women without migraine. The registry will identify and record pregnancy complications, major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births, and any other adverse outcomes, including postnatal growth and development. Outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.
